newsitem.title: UK: British election delays merger decisions.
newsitem.headline: British election delays merger decisions.

text.p: Britain's Department of Trade and Industry said on Monday it did not expect to make any decisions on British Airways Plc's planned alliance with AMR Corp's American Airlines until after national elections on May 1.
The mergers watchdog also said it did not plan to take any decisions on three merger reports, including Bass Plc's planned acquisition of Carlsberg-Tetley, before the election.
Earlier, the Monopolies and Mergers Commission confirmed that its findings on the Bass deal had gone to trade secretary Ian Lang.

The MMC was expected to report by April 4 on Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Co's planned ferry tie-up with Sweden's Stena Line AB and by April 17 on Klaus J. Jacobs Holding AG's planned acquisition of Societe Centrale D'Investissement et Associes.
Normally, Lang would be expected to make a decision on whether to wave a deal through in four to six weeks after delivery of an MMC report.

But Lang said he did not expect to take any decisions on merger cases after the scheduled dissolution of Parliament on April 8, except in a few situations. Bass shares fell 7.5 pence to close at 801.5, while BA slipped 5.0 pence to 631p ($10.11), and P&O ended the day down 9.0 pence at 624.5. ($ = 0.623 British Pounds)
